issues.t: Charging unit (ICCU) failure cuts drive power and kills the 12V battery (recall)
issues.sym: Often a loud pop from the rear, then warnings like "Check electrical system" or "Stop vehicle and check power supply". Power drops to limp mode (sometimes about 25 mph) or the car stops moving, and the 12-volt battery may go flat.
issues.why: The integrated charging control unit (ICCU) charges the small 12-volt battery from the big drive battery. Parts inside it can fail, and then the 12-volt system runs down and the car loses drive power. Kia recalled about 63,000 EV6s (NHTSA 24V-200, then 24V-867, which replaced it); some cars failed again after the first fix.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls even if one was already done, since the later recall covers previously repaired cars. If the warning appears while driving, get off the road safely and have the car towed to a dealer.

issues.t: High-voltage battery cells can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a problem. In rare cases, smoke or fire from under the car.
issues.why: Some cells in the drive battery may have misaligned electrodes, which can cause an internal short and a fire. NHTSA 26V-431 calls for replacing the whole high-voltage battery.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Until the free battery replacement is done, park outside away from buildings and limit charging to 80% as Kia advises.

issues.t: Drive shaft can break and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or bang and then the car stops pulling, even though the motor runs.
issues.why: Some drive shafts were not heat-treated correctly and can break under load. NHTSA 24V-057 covers certain 2023 EV6s and some Niro EVs.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the dealer replace the drive shaft for free.

issues.t: Car can roll away after being put in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car may move after it is shut off in Park.
issues.why: A voltage dip could make the shifter control unit release the parking mechanism. About 9,000 early 2022 cars were recalled (NHTSA 22V-322) for a software update.
issues.next: Get the free software update. Until then, park on level ground and use the parking brake.

issues.t: Sudden power loss from ICCU failure on 2025 models
issues.sym: A pop, a "check electrical system" or battery warning, and then the car slows to a crawl or loses drive power. The 12-volt battery may die, disabling hazards and door locks.
issues.why: Dealers have traced many 2025 power-loss cases to a failed ICCU, the same part behind the earlier recalls. Replacement parts are often backordered.
issues.next: Get safely off the road and have the car towed. Keep records of every visit; the part should be covered by Kia's EV warranty.

issues.sym: The car will not power on, shows "12V battery very low", or needs repeated jump starts, even after a battery replacement.
issues.why: The 12-volt battery keeps the car's computers alive. If the ICCU is not charging it properly, or something drains it while parked, it goes flat. Dealers sometimes find nothing wrong with the battery itself.
issues.next: Keep a portable jump pack. Ask the dealer to check the ICCU and its recalls, not just replace the battery, and to look for software updates.

issues.t: Charging stops or will not start
issues.sym: Home Level 2 charging stops with "Charge interrupted", charges slower than expected, or fast charging quits after a few minutes or will not start. Some owners also report trouble at Tesla Superchargers.
issues.why: Owners report charging faults from launch through 2025. Some were fixed by software updates; others were tied to the charging unit or never found.
issues.next: Try another charger to rule out the station. Make sure the car's software is up to date, then have the dealer check the charging system if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Charge port gets hot and charging slows or stops
issues.sym: The charge plug or port feels very hot and charging slows down or stops.
issues.why: Owners report overheating at the charge port. A Kia bulletin lowered the charging rate when overheating is detected, but owners say it does not fix the port or wiring.
issues.next: Stop charging if the plug is too hot to touch and check for damaged pins. Have the dealer inspect the port and wiring.

issues.t: Brake lights may not light during strong regenerative braking
issues.sym: The car slows hard in one-pedal or strong regen mode without the brake lights coming on.
issues.why: Owners report the brake lights do not light during heavy regenerative slowing, which can surprise drivers behind.
issues.next: Use the brake pedal in traffic when slowing quickly. Report it to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Navigation, app and screen glitches after software updates
issues.sym: Navigation stops showing charger availability, the Kia app loses charging network data, regen settings do not save, or new warnings appear after an update.
issues.why: Owners link these to over-the-air software updates.
issues.next: Restart the infotainment system and check for newer updates. Report persistent problems to the dealer.

issues.t: Rear door or keyless entry works only sometimes
issues.sym: A rear door will not open from time to time, or the car does not unlock as you walk up with the key fob.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent door and keyless entry faults, often alongside other electrical complaints.
issues.next: Use the physical key or app as a backup, and have the dealer check the door modules under warranty.

issues.t: Outside door handles make noise when they retract
issues.sym: A grinding or squeaking sound when the flush door handles pop out or retract.
issues.why: The push rod in the electric door handle actuator did not get enough grease at the factory. Kia bulletin BOD307 covers early 2022 GT-Line cars.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to apply bulletin BOD307 under warranty.

issues.t: Loud pop and power loss from burnt power electronics
issues.sym: A pop, loss of power and a car that will not shift out of Park or restart.
issues.why: In NHTSA complaints, dealers found the inverter burnt and charred on at least one 2024 car.
issues.next: Get away from the car if you see smoke, then have it towed. Report it to Kia and NHTSA.
